A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same inverse-dynamics and GRPO research, renamed from UIShift to GUI-Shift. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial experimental revisions.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.5 and Appendix B report original Qwen2.5-VL fine-tuning experiments, benchmark results and ablations.

after.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 and Appendices B–C report original experiments across Qwen, InternVL and MiMo backbones, including filtering and training-method comparisons.

M1.justification: v3 adds model-specific filtering that retains state pairs producing both correct and incorrect predictions among eight sampled responses; Qwen remains unfiltered. It also expands the action space from five to eight types, adding long_press, navigate_home and wait. These are substantive procedural changes, while the underlying inverse-dynamics task and GRPO objective remain.

E1.justification: v3 adds GUI Odyssey automation evaluation, including its tablet and cross-app scenarios, beyond v2's AndroidControl evaluation. AndroidControl and ScreenSpot-v2/Pro remain. Original ScreenSpot evaluation is removed, although mobile, desktop and web grounding coverage remains through ScreenSpot-v2.

E2.justification: The AndroidControl comparison adds GPT-4o, SeeClick, AgentCPM-GUI and UI-Venus-Navi-7B (v3 Table 1). Grounding comparisons add LPO and UI-Venus-Ground-7B, while UI-R1-3B and GUI-R1-7B disappear from the ScreenSpot-Pro comparison. These are changes in reported comparator membership, beyond extending existing comparators to GUI Odyssey.

E3.justification: Reported training changes from full-parameter fine-tuning for eight epochs on eight A800 GPUs to language-model-only optimization, with frozen vision encoder/projector, for four epochs on eight H100 GPUs. v3 replaces Qwen-3B experiments with InternVL3-8B and MiMo-7B variants and uses 2K samples per k instead of v2's predominantly 1K experiments plus selected 2K conditions.

E4.justification: v3 adds extensive filtered-versus-unfiltered analyses across models, transition distances and benchmarks, and expands SFT-versus-GRPO comparisons across k (Figures 2–3). It replaces v2's separate training/inference reasoning configurations with a training-reasoning comparison. The original grounding reasoning ablations and explicit 1K-versus-2K scaling analysis are absent.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v3's additional model variants and plots do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and supplemented. Qwen-7B, 2K, k=1 AndroidControl Low/High scores change from 86.0/55.2 in v2 Table 1 to 90.6/70.4 in v3 Table 1 under revised training conditions, so these are not established same-setting gains. New results cover GUI Odyssey, additional backbones and filtering. Retained baseline entries also change: UI-R1-E-3B's ScreenSpot-v2 mobile text/icon values are 98.2/83.9 in v2 Table 3 versus 83.0/97.1 in v3 Table 2.

T1.justification: The GRPO objective and additive reward remain unchanged, but v3 introduces a piecewise reward definition covering the expanded action space (Equation 3). As written, its click/long_press branch omits the explicit predicted-action-type equality required by v2's prose, creating a limited difference in the formal specification. Neither version presents theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central self-supervised inverse-dynamics claim remains, but the headline contributions are substantially refocused. v2 emphasizes reasoning dispensability, k=1's balanced performance and a claimed ScreenSpot-v2 state of the art. v3 foregrounds filtering, handling action multiplicity, generalization across four backbones and automation gains of up to 11.2 percentage points over base models.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of filtering as selecting learnable samples, explains its Qwen exception, and attributes some regressions to tablet layouts or high-resolution desktop inputs. It also emphasizes format mismatch when interpreting SFT failures. Conversely, v2's explicit small-training-set and static-evaluation limitations, and its recommendation to align k with task granularity, are removed.

D1.justification: v3 documents filtering mechanics and candidate-pool yield, the Qwen exception, evaluation toolkits and test-set sizes. However, it removes v2 Appendix C's exact training/evaluation prompts, the view-hierarchy instructions for extracting target bounding boxes, and the code/model/data access statement and repository link. Reproducibility documentation therefore changes substantially in both directions.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including UI-Venus, MiMo-VL, LPO and AgentCPM-GUI, while removing ScaleTrack and Perception-R1 discussion. It newly distinguishes UI-TARS's state-description task from action prediction. These update the comparisons and positioning, while retaining the broad relationship to annotation-dependent GUI training and rule-based RL.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodological explanations and conclusion are extensively rewritten alongside the UIShift-to-GUI-Shift renaming. Separate reasoning, training-task and transition-distance subsections are reorganized into a consolidated ablation section. The appendices change from hyperparameters, supplementary grounding results and prompts to hyperparameters and detailed automation/grounding analyses.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 1 and moves it into the introduction, adds multi-panel Figures 2–3, and substantially restructures the main and appendix tables. Tables gain model-family color bands and improvement/degradation arrows, while detailed transition-distance results move into expanded appendix displays. The original prompt boxes disappear.

improvement.justification: The broader backbone and GUI Odyssey evaluations, together with matched filtering and training-algorithm comparisons, provide stronger evidence about transferability and failure cases than v2's Qwen-only study. The net improvement is limited by removing exact prompts, release information and explicit limitations. Claim-table discrepancies also remain: v3's introduction assigns Qwen a 2.5-point ScreenSpot-v2 gain, whereas Table 2 reports 1.3 points.
